Sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a significant, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

In a recent development, heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.).

Industry observers note that broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Industry observers note that remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

Why Weed Might Actually Be Bad for Your Sleep

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that everyone’s done it before.
  • Industry observers note that the study, which was performed by Northwestern University researchers and published in JAMA Network, looked at 1,266 adults who participated in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study, which followed participants for 35 years to determine how behavioral, biological, and environmental factors affected their risk of heart disease later in life.
  • Here’s what all of that means: Sleep efficiency is essentially how much of the time you spend in bed you’re actually asleep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that everyone’s done it before. A pre-game gummy. A nighttime toke. Weed is, at this point, a widely used sleep aid. It usually works pretty well, too. But if you’ve made it a habit, you might just be sabotaging your shut-eye in the long run. According to a new October 2026 study, consuming pot in any form before bed causes people to have poorer quality of sleep—without them even realizing it. In other words: It has exactly the opposite of its intended effect. Here’s what you should know before popping an edible before you doze off.

Industry observers note that the study, which was performed by Northwestern University researchers and published in JAMA Network, looked at 1,266 adults who participated in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study, which followed participants for 35 years to determine how behavioral, biological, and environmental factors affected their risk of heart disease later in life. Of that sample size, 891 wore wrist-based activity monitors for at least a week so that researchers could examine their sleep patterns. After analyzing the data, the researchers found that those who were long-term cannabis owners had “poorer objective sleep, including lower sleep efficiency, greater fragmentation, and more time awake during the night,” Dr. Thanh-Huyen Vu, an author of the study and a research associate professor of preventive medicine at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine, tells GQ.

Here’s what all of that means: Sleep efficiency is essentially how much of the time you spend in bed you’re actually asleep. So, lower sleep efficiency means spending more time lying awake instead of sleeping while sleep fragmentation refers to how often your sleep is interrupted, like when you’re unknowingly tossing and turning to get comfortable. The researchers also looked at how much total time participants spent awake during the night. It all boils down to the fact that long-term cannabis users weren’t sleeping as soundly or as continuously throughout the night—sometimes without them even knowing it.

According to recent reports, the researchers can’t say for certain. Because the study was observational, it only established an association between long-term cannabis exposure and poorer sleep quality.

One possibility, Vu suggests, is that cannabis may “alter normal sleep architecture,” potentially changing the way the body cycles through different sleep stages.

According to recent reports, over time, it’s those changes that can contribute to more nighttime awakenings, which result in less restorative sleep. She says more research is needed to understand the underlying biological mechanisms.

In a recent development, deep sleep is one of the most important stages of sleep because it’s the phase when your body recovers physically, processes memory, and regulates the immune system. Interruptions in sleep result in less time during the deep sleep cycle, which inhibits your body from doing all the important things that help you function properly when you’re awake. The less deep sleep you get, the worse you feel in the morning. The reason why participants don’t pick up on these mid-sleep wake-ups is that they’re easy to forget. “Sleep trackers can capture some of these patterns, even when people don’t perceive their sleep as being particularly poor,” Vu says. It’s the same way in which you think you slept eight hours one night but woke up feeling groggy regardless.

Not necessarily. Given the sample population—middle-aged adults—the results may not apply to people in other age ranges or even those who use cannabis for medical reasons. Still, Vu states it’s key for people to understand that cannabis’s relationship with sleep may be more complicated than simply helping you drift off faster.

Recent findings suggest that if you regularly use cannabis before bed, paying attention to your sleep patterns may help you better understand how it’s affecting you. Wearable sleep trackers can offer some insight into nighttime awakenings and sleep efficiency, but you won’t get the same sleep analysis if you were part of a study like this. It might be worth trying out a period where you don’t use weed to fall asleep to see if it makes a difference in whether you feel more well-rested, or your mind feels sharper. Though the study still leaves a lot of questions to be answered, its data is clear enough to make anyone with a nightly gummy habit reconsider.

In this competitive environment, small brands with a focused, strategic approach can appear larger than life, while market leaders resting on their laurels could see their relevance shrink.

However, traditional discovery channels are proving resilient in the watch industry. Brand-owned websites remain the top destination for information and latest brand or product discovery, despite the rise of social media. The challenge is to turn digital visibility into engagement through strong direct-to-consumer (DTC) websites and a seamless omnichannel experience.

It has been revealed that in our digital analysis for the 2026 Vogue Business Watch Index, while the crown once again goes to Cartier, the ranking demonstrates several changes and surprises, notably IWC’s rise and Rolex’s slide. Due to the unavailability of data this year, Vogue Business has removed its review of performance on Chinese social media platforms WeChat, Xiaohongshu and Weibo as part of its methodology update. And while brands continuously refine their tactics on well-established — yet always evolving — digital platforms, it’s also key to track emerging ones that are rapidly capturing the public’s attention.

It has been revealed that in this year’s index, Hublot delivers a standout performance, jumping seven positions in the digital ranking vs. 2025 and landing just outside the top five. The key contributors to Hublot’s ascent are its robust digital services, which include a comprehensive omnichannel experience, and its Instagram performance. The brand has seen follower and engagement growth through content created in collaboration with its roster of ambassadors spanning sports and art.

IWC has considerably strengthened its position in the top five, advancing three places and landing second behind Cartier, thanks to exceptional social media performance, particularly on Facebook, where its engineering- and Formula 1-focused content continues to resonate. Omega slipped one place to third, yet remained a strong digital performer. The brand is strong on Instagram, TikTok and WeChat, and its Google Search visibility has increased year-on-year.

Meanwhile, despite its strong awareness and about 185 million Google visits from September 2025 to August 2026, Rolex slipped from third place in 2025 to fifth this year, due to insufficient activity, particularly on TikTok, where the brand has over 230,000 followers.

Sources indicate that longines’s fall from fourth to ninth place stands out. Historically, it’s a brand that performed well on Chinese platforms like Xiaohongshu and WeChat. However, its modest visibility on Western social media channels drags down its overall performance this year and highlights the need to deliver a consistent message across all geographies.

Recent findings suggest that A granular analysis of the overall digital ranking unveils that each brand has its own specific strengths and weaknesses. Yet a dichotomy emerges between brands with strong digital visibility and those that can integrate that digital visibility into omnichannel customer service activities that may ultimately lead to commercial transactions.

According to recent reports, the brands that perform best for digital, for example with high levels of engagement and interaction, are not always the brands that consumers rate highly for digital experience. For the most part, our consumer research highlights that opinions of content generally lag behind a more positive perception of the overall digital experience, with Tudor showing the biggest gap between the two.

Although Hublot ranks sixth in the overall digital ranking, it still has room to improve its omnichannel digital services. The brand boasts an innovative club-like loyalty program known as Hublotista, open to all Hublot watch owners; it offers live chats and click-and-collect options. However, other elements, such as product personalization and live inventory availability, trail competitors. Hublot is also the top performer on Instagram, but it ranks 15th in its Google Search traffic score. This means the brand excels at creating visibility and capitalizing on it through services, but it still has room to improve its equity in overall desirability.

Sources indicate that while Omega sits at 89% and third in the digital ranking, its omnichannel services have significant scope for growth. Although it has several customer service options, some more dynamic offerings, like loyalty programs, live inventories, and product customization, could be strengthened. In contrast, Panerai performs well on omnichannel for a brand of its size, coming in third for this assessment with its Panerai Passport service, WhatsApp customer service option and strong online-offline integration, but its digital performance on socials is significantly behind others, putting it at 18th overall for digital. Meanwhile, Richemont-owned Piaget ranks 16th overall for digital, driven by poorer exposure on Google Search and TikTok, but places fifth for omnichannel with a strong range of customer service options, click-and-collect and pre-order options.

But it’s Rolex that shows the most drastic dichotomy. The undisputed market leader, it generated a total turnover of CHF 11 billion ($13.1 billion) in 2025, up 4% from 2024, and commands a market share of 32.9%, followed by Cartier (8.7%), Patek Philippe (7%) and Omega (6.4%). The brand also tops the YouTube ranking and is the second most-searched brand on Google, behind Cartier. Yet while Rolex ranks fifth overall for digital performance, it is 17th for omnichannel services. Its absence from TikTok and limited digital services, which the brand typically hands over to its distributors rather than managing directly, weigh on its performance.

Sources indicate that services generally rank high among respondents’ preferences. Real-time product availability both in-store and online is the most sought-after service for 79%, followed by multiple channels of customer service (email, phone, messenger) at 76%, buying from the brand’s website at 74%, and the ability to speak directly to a brand advisor (phone, video, live chat) when shopping online at 73%. The possibility to pay in local currency far outweighs cryptocurrency (70% vs 26%), although crypto matters more for 41% of older Gen Z and younger millennials aged 25-34. All the services highlighted imply the importance of human contact and physical presence, which are also common denominators for brand experiences — the other most important development that excites consumers (alongside limited-edition timepieces).

Sources indicate that since the early 2000s, when Google Search began to rise in the digital world, search engine optimization (SEO) has been front and center in brands’ digital preoccupations, ensuring their products are easily found on Google and placed at the top of consumers’ search results. Websites, e-commerce platforms and digital campaigns are now built to match SEO criteria. But Google’s dominance is eroding and, with it, the foundations of brands’ digital strategies are starting to wobble, as consumers flock to AI-driven chatbots where GEO (generative engine optimization) becomes the newly introduced metric to please.

The watch industry is still, by and large, a sector that relies on traditional modes of discovery. Brand websites are the top channel for both sourcing information and discovering upcoming brands or products, highlighting how crucial it is for brands to have robust DTC websites. This is reinforced by the fact that, on average across all brands, nearly half (47.8%) of consumers who purchased watches in the last year bought directly from the brand. When researching watches, word-of-mouth recommendations and review sites or discussion forums rank among the top five channels, alongside search engines and magazines.

When it comes to discovering upcoming products or brands, however, magazines and social media play an influential role, as do monobrand stores and flagships. Yet in the fast-changing digital landscape, new modes of discovery are becoming increasingly ingrained in shopping habits, and preferred purchasing channels are shifting, with the average number of people using resale rising from 29.7% who shopped in the last year to 40.8% of those intending to buy in the coming year.

According to a Bain & Manufacturer study published in March, 56% of US-based consumers still resort to Google, but 16% already mostly or always use AI chatbots and 28% mix the two. But adoption of AI chatbots is stronger among Gen Z (25% mostly or always use chatbots and 33% mix the two), millennials (24% mostly or always use chatbots and 34% mix the two), and Gen X (14% mostly or always use chatbots and 31% mix the two). Thirty-three per cent of consumers already use AI chatbots for recommendations in general and 19% for shopping assistance specifically.

In this context, some brands have started to adapt. Nomos Glashütte, an independent watch brand based in the German watchmaking cluster that is also home to Richemont-owned A. Lange & Söhne, has begun updating its website to ensure AI chatbots can read it correctly and surface the brand’s products in their recommendations.

Sources indicate that analysts consider a website overhaul the easiest component of GEO brands can act on; the others remain much harder to control. AI chatbots draw information not only from brands’ websites but also from articles published in legacy media, typically sorted by readership and prestige. This is an element brands can influence through old-school public relations activity, but it is not fully under their sway. The third component is even more elusive: consumers’ comments on social media.

While brands practice “social listening” to improve on public feedback, they still can’t control people’s opinions and messages. But such comments are increasingly finding their way into AI chatbots, and they predominantly come from social media that are still newly introduced territory for brands: Reddit and Substack.

Sources indicate that A 2025 survey of Gen Zs, conducted by Vogue Business and youth culture agency Archrival, found that 65% of respondents use Reddit to find and discover products, valuing the platform’s privacy and the ability to ask questions anonymously. Vogue Business also highlighted that users typically spend longer on Reddit’s detailed threads than they do on other social platforms.

AI visibility is rapidly gaining relevance. Launchmetrics launched a fresh AI Visibility metric alongside its usual proprietary Media Impact Value. According to the firm’s analysis of brand mentions by AI during the Watches and Wonders fair, “being liked and being mentioned are two different things in AI. Tudor and Panerai come up far less often in AI answers, but when they do appear, they’re described so positively that it impacts their overall rank to third and fourth overall.”.

In a recent development, IWC achieves an impressive 95% score and lands in second place in the digital marketing ranking behind Cartier, as its laser-focused video strategy, highlighting a few key messages, delivers significant results. The Schaffhausen-headquartered brand is best-performing on Facebook with a score of 93%; second best on TikTok with 90%, behind Cartier (95%); and on YouTube with 89%, behind Rolex (92%).

Recent findings suggest that the brand’s message, anchored in engineering excellence and innovation, is articulated through its association with Formula 1 and a few well-selected ambassadors who don’t simply pose wearing a timepiece but get involved in brand-related projects. IWC also regularly features videos of its watchmakers assembling timepieces. One filming Florian Salzer working on the Ingenieur Tourbillon 41 IWC345901 amassed over 10 million views and over half a million likes on TikTok alone.

IWC also runs the successful series “IWC Replies”, in which watchmakers answer technical questions asked by the community, like “Would the perpetual calendar still work after 2299?”.

It has been revealed that this year, IWC released a series of timepieces co-designed with George Russell, a driver for the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 team. The watch was made in the racing team’s blue hue, engraved on the back with Russell’s number 63, and Russell himself featured in the social media campaign. The brand has previously collaborated with supermodel Gisele Bündchen, who was not only an ambassador but an environmental and community projects advisor. The brand playfully mixes engineering-focused content with ambassador-led storytelling. One TikTok video featuring Russell’s teammate, Kimi Antonelli, assembling a timepiece achieved half a million views, proving the appeal of involving the brand’s “myth-makers” in the watchmaking process.

Videos of IWC’s watchmakers at work have helped the brand rise three places to second in this year’s Index.

IWC also explores content related to travel where precision matters, like space travel and aviation. This year, the brand is collaborating with Vast to test timepieces during space flights. In a more poetic vein, the brand also released a new Pilot’s Watch celebrating the 20th anniversary of its association with the foundation linked to author and aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, who wrote the children’s tale of the space traveler The Little Prince.

Managing director, Ulysse Nardin.

According to recent reports, while many watchmakers still value traditional media, Ulysse Nardin has embraced social media and made it a pillar of its communications strategy. Why?

According to recent reports, continuous improvement is obviously a must, but in brand-building, it is not enough. There are many elements of brand-building we could choose to focus on, but not all would deliver the same impact. With all the money in the world, I don’t think we could revolutionize the in-store customer experience and move the needle for our brand.

Sources indicate that but social media is still a blue ocean, in the sense that small investments can deliver impactful, meaningful results. But you need to know the rules of the game. The type of content that is consumed and thrives on social media is made by content creators, not the polished content by luxury brands. People relate to people, and partnering with content creators is paramount.

We asked ourselves: how can we go viral and put our iconic Freak watch in the minds of millions of people with minimal investment?

According to recent reports, we noticed that food-related content was getting a lot of traction, so we decided to collaborate with chocolate specialist Amaury Guichon, who is half Swiss and half French. The video of him making a giant chocolate sculpture of the Freak watch was watched by half a billion people. Amaury Guichon is now a friend of the brand, and we featured him in our UNstoppable campaign on social media, which celebrates the achievements of extraordinary people.

And you managed to have a significant impact at Watches and Wonders with dancing robots. Tell us more about that.

One of the brand’s pillars, which is transversal across all our activities, is our mission to inspire innovation.

Sources indicate that we knew that at Watches and Wonders, we did not want to be confined to a box and mark our presence on the whole fair. Renting two robots, which cost us less than a page of advertising in a glossy magazine, proved a very effective way to achieve our objective. We dressed them in sweaters celebrating the 25th anniversary of the Freak watch. As they greeted guests and danced, many visitors stopped to take pictures of them and share them on social media. The visitors became our spontaneous content creators.

Ulysse Nardin’s dancing robots at Watches and Wonders cost less than a magazine ad page and turned visitors into the brand’s content creators.

We spent no money on advertising at Watches and Wonders, but we had a major impact. Thanks to these unconventional actions, the Freak watch has become a pillar of the brand, accounting for about 50% of total turnover.

The Vogue Business Watch Index examines watchmakers’ digital activity across 48 social media platforms: the Western trinity of Facebook, Instagram and YouTube as well as the global China-native TikTok. A separate score is assigned for search volumes on Google, as well as for the digital services offered by the brands. All these scores are weighted to produce a final digital ranking.

Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

In a recent development, preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Industry observers note that arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a substantial pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

Should You Worry About That Bump on Your Chest?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that while male breast cancer is rare, estimates suggest that more than 2,600 men are diagnosed with an invasive form of the disease each year in the United States, and more than 500 die, according to the American Cancer Society.
  • Sources indicate that there isn’t a universal description of what breast cancer lumps look like in men, but there are some common characteristics to keep in mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re like most guys, you probably have plenty of little bumps and lumps on your skin. There’s the callus on your toe from training for that 10K, the razor bumps along your neck from this morning’s shave, and the skin tag on your underarm you keep meaning to get removed. While it’s often completely fine to ignore these bumps, that isn’t always the case. Some can be a red flag worth paying attention to—especially if they’re on your chest.

It has been revealed that while male breast cancer is rare, estimates suggest that more than 2,600 men are diagnosed with an invasive form of the disease each year in the United States, and more than 500 die, according to the American Cancer Society. And one of its telltale signs is a firm bump under or near your nipple. Below, find out more about what a breast-cancer lump may look like and four other things that could be to blame for a new bump on your chest.

Sources indicate that there isn’t a universal description of what breast cancer lumps look like in men, but there are some common characteristics to keep in mind. “Breast cancer in men typically presents as a painless, firm, or hard lump,” states Jose Pablo Leone, MD, the director of the Program for Breast Cancer in Men at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston.

Another sign that the bump could be breast cancer is if it’s behind or very close to the nipple and areola. “Men have much less developed breast glandular tissue than women, which is why breast cancer in men most commonly develops near or behind the nipple,” indicates Dr. Leone. As for size even a lump as small as a pea can be cancerous, but by the time men go to the doctor, tumors are often larger than a marble, according to Dr. Leone. “In part because of the lack of awareness and screening, most men present with larger tumors,” he says. “But any size is worth mentioning to your doctor. Not all breast cancers feel the same, so any newly introduced or persistent breast lump should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.”.

Your chest has a lot of oil glands, which can set the stage for pimples. “Staying in a sweaty shirt after a workout can make chest acne flare, especially if the fabric is tight and rubs against your skin,” notes Elizabeth Bahar Houshmand, MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in Dallas. While blackheads and whiteheads are typically small and easy to identify, inflamed pimples or nodules may seem more alarming because they can be hard, painful, and form deep under the skin. When it comes to nodular acne specifically, you can’t treat it on your own. If that’s what you think you’re dealing with, see a dermatologist, who can prescribe an oral or topical medication to help clear it up.

It has been revealed that “This is a collection of fat that forms under the skin,” says Sonya Kenkare, MD, a board-certified dermatologist at Illinois Dermatology Institute in Hinsdale, Illinois. “It is usually soft, not painful, and you can move it around in all different directions.” You don’t need to do anything about a lipoma, but if you want to get it removed, you can talk to a doctor about it.

Industry observers note that when hair follicles get inflamed or infected, you can end up with folliculitis. “Folliculitis often looks like small pimples or pus-filled bumps centered around a hair follicle” claims Dr. Houshmand. “They may itch or feel tender.”.

It has been revealed that blockage or damage to a hair follicle can also cause epidermal inclusion cysts. These cysts occur when dead skin cells get trapped under the surface instead of shedding. “They feel somewhat firm and often have a central little black spot,” says Dr. Kenkare. Sometimes simply applying a warm compress to the area can help a cyst heal on its own, but a doctor can also inject it with a steroid to reduce swelling, drain it, or surgically remove it.

This condition occurs when breast tissue gets enlarged in men, and it can first appear as a lump under your nipple. “It often feels like a rubbery or firm disc beneath the nipple, and it may be tender,” indicates Dr. Houshmand. While gynecomastia can come on as a side effect of some medications, like antibiotics or antidepressants, or diseases like thyroid disorders, sometimes there is no clear cause at all.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re starting to feel like it’s difficult to tell on your own what the lump on your chest might be, you’re not wrong. That’s why it’s best to have your primary care physician look at any upcoming, unexplained bumps and tell you whether you need imaging, like a mammogram with an ultrasound. That may sound scary, but it’s really just covering your bases. “Uncommon things are uncommon, and breast cancer in men is uncommon,” says Dr. Leone. “You shouldn’t worry excessively about male breast cancer, but you should be aware of it.”.

The Best Frozen Lasagna, According to Our Taste Test

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, frozen lasagna is a meal for when you just don’t have it in you.
  • For this taste test, we sampled nine varieties of store-bought meat lasagna, cooking each from frozen and concealing the brand names from our tasters.
  • After grumbling our way through several contenders and questioning mankind’s ability to produce a decent supermarket lasagna, Trader Giotto’s Family Style Meat Lasagna restored our faith with a hearty meat sauce and genuinely tasty noodles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, frozen lasagna is a meal for when you just don’t have it in you. For when you need the comfort of pasta, cheese, and sauce, but you’re not prepared to spend hours boiling, sautéing, and layering. And that’s okay. A great frozen lasagna might not hold a candle to BA’s Best Lasagna, but at the very least it should hold together, with distinct layers, plenty of sauce, gooey cheese, and bouncy pasta.

For this taste test, we sampled nine varieties of store-bought meat lasagna, cooking each from frozen and concealing the brand names from our tasters. Three stood out: Trader Joe’s tasted the closest to homemade, Marie Callender’s was a solid backup, and Rao’s was our favorite for a single serving.

After grumbling our way through several contenders and questioning mankind’s ability to produce a decent supermarket lasagna, Trader Giotto’s Family Style Meat Lasagna restored our faith with a hearty meat sauce and genuinely tasty noodles.

Why it won us over: Trader Joe’s frozen lasagna had a homemade vibe. There were distinct layers of pasta, cheese, and meaty sauce. The cheeses—ricotta, mozzarella, Romano, and Parmesan—each pulled their weight. And the noodles had a fresh bounce. “There’s a whole tomato!” exclaimed senior editor Kelsey Jane Youngman upon finding a chunk of diced tomato in her sample. Other tasters complimented the bright aromatics—fennel was prominent, backed up by oregano and basil. The evenly distributed ground beef and pork were the cherry on top.

Trader Giotto’s Family-Style Meat Lasagna, 32-oz.

More great frozen foods at Trader Joe’s →.

Big Lasagna would have you believe you’ll always want to cook a frozen lasagna for a crowd, but sometimes it’s about you and you alone. The 9-oz. Rao’s Made for Home Meat Lasagna is just enough for a single serving—and it doesn’t sacrifice flavor.

Sources indicate that why it won us over: Our tasters were excited to report that Rao’s delivered on structure. While other lasagnas were soupy, floppy, or otherwise unbalanced, Rao’s stayed intact, layer on top of layer, as we ate. It had sturdy (but not tough) noodles, a tomato sauce that was full of umami, and herbal accents that didn’t overpower. Some tasters noted a robust beefy flavor; others were more focused on the garlic and onion. Everyone went in for a second bite.

Rao’s Made-for-Home Meat Lasagna, 9-oz.

According to recent reports, maybe you don’t live by a Trader Joe’s—our condolences—and Rao’s proves elusive. You still deserve a serviceable frozen lasagna. Marie Callender’s Lasagna With Meat Sauce offers a sweet and tangy tomato sauce punctuated by well-seasoned meat and noodles that hold their shape.

Recent findings suggest that why it won us over: This contender avoided many of the pitfalls other brands fell into. It had a solid tomato sauce that was just slightly sweet and tangy, and the meat—both beef and sausage—was flavorful and varied enough in size to give each bite some dynamism. The pasta sheets were springy, not gummy. And while it wasn’t drowning in dairy, there was enough cottage cheese and mozzarella to make itself known.

Marie Callender’s Lasagna With Meat Sauce, 10.5-oz.

Industry observers note that we cooked each lasagna from frozen according to its package instructions. While most contenders offered both oven and microwave directions, we stuck with the oven. Tasters sampled each lasagna without knowing which brand they were trying, evaluating each for flavor, texture, and structural integrity. Although Giovanni Rana’s Meat Lasagna is sold refrigerated, we froze it before baking, following the brand’s instructions for cooking from frozen.

The best frozen lasagna should deliver on the fundamentals of structure, flavor, and texture—a tall order for many of our contenders. That meant distinct layers; sheets of pasta that were bouncy, not flimsy; tomato sauce with concentrated flavor and enough body to cling to the pasta; meat that stood out instead of getting lost; and cheese—or many cheeses—that added milky flavor and melty cohesion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

In a recent development, if you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

In a recent development, in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Industry observers note that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

Gifting, Resale and the Power of Experiences: The Watch Industry Is in Its Customer Service Era

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mixture of high-level customer service, personal experiences, and frictionless shopping has helped watchmakers improve their image and perceived value among consumers this year.
  • Industry observers note that watch brands’ awareness among consumers is on the rise, and this moves in lockstep with overall positive associations.
  • Despite pressure from higher gold prices and a strong Swiss franc that has forced watchmakers to raise prices across the board in recent years, respondents still consider watches a good investment, increasingly purchase them as gifts, and remain loyal to their brands of choice even when confronted with price rises.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mixture of high-level customer service, personal experiences, and frictionless shopping has helped watchmakers improve their image and perceived value among consumers this year.

Industry observers note that watch brands’ awareness among consumers is on the rise, and this moves in lockstep with overall positive associations. In this scenario, established brands have strengthened their position, while smaller brands have found fertile ground to grow.

Despite pressure from higher gold prices and a strong Swiss franc that has forced watchmakers to raise prices across the board in recent years, respondents still consider watches a good investment, increasingly purchase them as gifts, and remain loyal to their brands of choice even when confronted with price rises.

The recent excitement around resale schemes, limited editions, in-person services, immediate stock availability and exhibitions spotlights an appetite for proximity, access and the human touch, offering opportunities for brands that can support customers across multiple touchpoints and build communities.

At the top of the innovation table, the best performers — Rolex, Cartier, Omega, Patek Philippe, and Tag Heuer — each maintained their position in the 2026 Vogue Business Watch Index, even improving their score. Rolex keeps its crown for overall consumer sentiment, achieving 99% aided awareness, and Tag Heuer boosts its aided awareness score by 2 percentage points. Despite Breitling, in sixth position, improving its overall brand awareness ranking from 72% to 73%, driven by improvements in aided awareness, the gap with Tag Heuer for overall awareness widened to 8 percentage points.

The most striking result of the Index is that 75% of the brands surveyed have seen their awareness score improve, bringing the overall average awareness score up by 1.6 percentage points, which means the public is more aware of the watch category as a whole and readily recognizes brands.

Recent findings suggest that chopard takes the crown as the top performer by improving its awareness score by 6 percentage points from 62% last year to 68% this year. It is followed by Longines, A. Lange & Söhne, and Vacheron Constantin, which improved by 4 percentage points, and Piaget, Audemars Piguet, IWC, and Movado, which improved their score by 3 percentage points.

Interestingly, this year the top five brands improved their overall awareness (combined aided and unaided awareness) score by 1 percentage point to an average of 90%, while the other 15 surveyed brands registered a higher increase of 1.8 percentage points. This means the challengers are putting more pressure on the top five, but with an average aggregated awareness of 58.4%, the gap is still wide.

The awareness ranking is particularly relevant because it indicates a strong correlation with brand equity, consumer sentiment, and purchase intent, particularly for the top five performers.

But awareness alone does not translate into purchase intent across the board, as purchase intent far lags awareness. Rolex, the top performer, ranked first across all criteria, has only 38% purchase intent, but in a ranking methodology, becomes the “100%” player to which all other brands are indexed. Across the board, purchase intent is relatively flat vs. last year, with actual purchase intent sitting at 16% on average across all brands. This means that brands with relatively modest purchase intent, such as A. Lange & Söhne at 14%, perform above average when ranked (coming in at 58% in the ranking), given the economic pressures on purchase intent. Yet this methodology does expose just how competitive the landscape is. When we rank purchase intent, A. Lange & Söhne is comparable to IWC, despite the latter enjoying significantly higher brand awareness, with aided awareness sitting 25 percentage points higher. In contrast, brands such as Breitling, Hublot and Tudor display high awareness ranking scores (Breitling 73%, Hublot 66%, and Tudor 49%) but actual purchase intent of just 12% and 13%.

Interestingly, brand loyalty has increased to 64.3% vs 63% last year, as consumers resist the temptation to switch to a more affordable brand even if prices increase, with the 45-64 age group having the strongest resolve. Nevertheless, that same demographic demonstrates a higher propensity to explore discounts and resale options, still showing some price sensitivity.

In 2025, Vogue Business asked luxury watch consumers about their watch-buying habits for gifting occasions in the Middle East. This year, we extended that question to all markets. The results reveal interesting motives for buying luxury timepieces, as well as how this varies by local culture.

Overall, key occasions include birthdays (34.1%), Valentine’s Day (29.7%) and Christmas (27.6%), as well as weddings and engagements, particularly for Gen Z (30%) and Gen X (31%). Interestingly, the 40% of luxury consumers who spend more on luxury watches (over $5,000 in the last five years) show a higher propensity to buy luxury watches as gifts for others across every occasion.

Industry observers note that self-gifting has also become a prevalent trend. China is the leading market for personal birthday buys, at 55%, compared with 32% when buying for others. In the Middle East, self-purchasing for birthdays sits at just 32%. Instead, Eid is the leading self-gifting occasion, at 38% — far outpacing buying for others at 24%. This indicates many shoppers are taking advantage of seasonal deals for their own interests. The self-gifting trend also reveals interesting behavior for romantic occasions: a fifth (20%) of luxury consumers in the UK say they have bought themselves luxury watches as an anniversary present in the last two years — double the percentage of French consumers who’ve done the same (10%). Curiously, the opposite is true for weddings and engagements, where only 10% of UK luxury watch consumers shop for this occasion, but 17% of French consumers do. This shows how nuanced gifting occasions are by market, and how the hierarchy of milestones and relationships differs across cultures.

For many years, watch brands have pursued partnerships with the automotive industry, but lately this association seems to be influencing the watchmaking business model, which is increasingly leaning toward the car-making industry’s emphasis on service, a greater focus on experiences and integrated resale options.

When it comes to executing the latter, interestingly, it is the youngest, independent brands such as Richard Mille, MB&F, F.P.Journe and Urwerk that have grasped the importance of owning their secondary market, which leads not only to better control over prices and the products’ retained value but also promotes proximity to clients who, in turn, tend to be more loyal to the brand, act as natural ambassadors, and form communities.

The launch of certified pre-owned schemes has been one of the most significant milestones in the watch industry. While Cartier pioneered the concept in the 1990s, other watch specialists such as Vacheron Constantin and Rolex joined only in the last five years. At the end of October, Audemars Piguet introduced its “Watch Keepers”, its own certified pre-owned program, which will operate as a digital platform enabling sales at a fixed price as well as auctions. It is launching in Europe and Switzerland first before expanding into the United States.

Brand-owned retail platforms allow brands to retain customers who are loyal to the brand but seek more cost-effective options when prices rise. It’s a concern that affects nearly half of all luxury watch consumers, at 47%, with this rising by age as older shoppers say they will shop more for sales and discounts.

Last year’s Vogue Business Watch Index highlighted how brands with low awareness scores were associated with strong purchase intent. This insight is driving brands to purposefully cultivate their niche and strengthen their bond with clients through ad hoc partnerships, without venturing into high-cost, high-visibility collaborations.

The most interesting success story is that of A. Lange & Söhne because, unlike all other brands surveyed, it is not Swiss but German — and its history, which began in 1845 in Glashütte, stalled between 1945 and 1990, when the brand was relaunched.

From the start, A. Lange & Söhne has cultivated its difference, expanded organically, and gradually grown its base of collectors and buyers with a laser focus on products and selected partnerships. The brand forged strong links early on with prestigious cultural institutions in Dresden, the capital of Saxony, where Glashütte is located. These include the brand’s support for the Dresden State Art Collections (Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden) and the Semperoper opera house, which have run for over 20 years. As part of these tie-ups, the brand supported the exhibition “Paula Modersohn-Becker and Edvard Munch. The Massive Questions of Life” this year. Such partnerships show collectors who visit the brand’s manufacture how the brand is deeply interwoven into the cultural fabric of the area it comes from.

It has been revealed that more recently, A. Lange & Söhne has built on that art legacy by partnering with car events such as the Concours d’Elegance in Hampton Court (UK), Como (Italy) and Newport, Rhode Island (US), known as Audrain Newport Concours & Motor Week. At the end of 2025, the brand opened two newly introduced stores, one in London and one in Singapore, while in June this year, it opened its first store in Lisbon.

Other brands following this approach are Jaeger-LeCoultre, with 58% aided awareness, Piaget at 70% awareness, and IWC at 59%. For these brands, criteria such as “its products are a good investment”, “interesting story brand”, and “heritage” seemed to move the needle strongly in consumers’ perceptions.

Sources indicate that these brands have all followed the same restrained and laser-focused blueprint. Boasting an uninterrupted history since its founding in 1833 in Le Sentier, Switzerland, Jaeger-LeCoultre has privileged experiences and exhibitions. At the end of last year, the brand inaugurated its installation “The Dream Shaper” in Shanghai, which showcased over 70 archival pieces and celebrated the brand’s heritage in crafting ladies’ watches. The event was attended by the brand’s ambassadors, including South Korean actor Kim Woo-bin. This year, Jaeger-LeCoultre celebrated its signature Reverso design with a series of dedicated in-store experiences, “Reverso Stories”, as well as some limited-edition pieces presented during Homo Faber in Venice in September.

It has been revealed that piaget has strengthened its commitment to the arts by renewing its partnership with The Andy Warhol Foundation, which led to newly introduced limited-edition pieces this year. The brand also sponsors the Prix Solo Art Genève, a prize awarded to the best solo show during Art Genève. Meanwhile, IWC has cultivated its difference by continuing its association with Formula 1 and highlighting the uniqueness of its heritage with the launch of IWC. Curated — since the end of 2025, some IWC watches from the Maison’s museum have been selected for reproduction and sold in limited quantities.

In a recent development, cartier staged the second part of its brand exhibition in Melbourne, Australia; Panerai unveiled a showcase in its hometown of Florence, while Patek Philippe brought its retrospective exhibition to Milan. The exhibition, which ran from October 2-18, showcased over 500 pieces and attracted 68,000 visitors. Analysts agree that such exhibitions not only boost the brand equity of the company organizing them, but also increase the general public’s interest in watchmaking.

This year’s most significant trend was the relaunch of milestone designs that ticked most of the boxes that get consumers excited, namely vintage, heritage and limited editions.

One of the most recent examples is Hublot’s Classic Fusion Tributo, which the brand developed with its founder, Carlo Crocco, who also served as the unofficial ambassador for the occasion, marking the first time he has collaborated with Hublot since selling it to LVMH in 2008.

The new watch, released in October in Milan this year, is an almost identical reproduction of the model that made Hublot famous in 1980. It features a gold case with screws that also serve as hour indices, mounted on a black rubber strap that, thanks to technological advances, is odorless and does not need to be infused with vanilla like the original 1980s version. The launch allowed clients to meet the brand’s founder and hear directly from him how the watch ended up on the wrist of King Constantine II of Greece, who also gifted one to his brother-in-law, King Juan Carlos of Spain, among other illustrious personalities such as Princess Caroline of Monaco, Elton John and Giorgio Armani.

Hublot’s executive team told the press at the launch that Gen Z’s interest in vintage pieces with a small dial prompted them to launch the project three years early, ahead of the model’s 50th anniversary.

Chopard’s relaunch of the original Happy Diamonds watch also marks the celebration of its 50th anniversary. At a party during New York Fashion Week hosted by brand ambassador Bella Hadid, Chopard introduced the new Happy Sport Heritage, reproducing the original cushion-shaped, golden case framing an onyx dial over which diamonds float freely, and mounted on a black leather strap. Chopard also seized the opportunity to relaunch the original Happy Sport designed in 1993 by the creative director and co-president Caroline Scheufele. Happy Sport was conceived as an evolution of the original Happy Diamonds watch and marked the first time diamonds were paired with steel.

CEO, Watches of Switzerland Group.

In your latest annual report, client experience is mentioned as a growth pillar. What does it mean?

It has been revealed that watches of Switzerland excels in two very different categories: one-time buyers and serial collectors who own hundreds of timepieces. This means we have to offer a variety of services to satisfy the very different demands of these two groups.

Sources indicate that for example, those who only buy one or two watches in their lives may welcome our financing options, as well as the education our salespeople provide to help them buy with confidence something they can treasure and pass on. For dedicated collectors, we focus on providing access to exceptional timepieces and bringing them closer to the brands and the world of watchmaking.

According to recent reports, we regularly treat our best clients to manufacturer visits, take them to watch fairs such as Watches and Wonders, and secure exceptional watches. For example, this week, we are inviting them to discover all the timepieces recognized with prestigious GPHG watchmaking awards (Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève), including the independent Rexhep Rexhepi and the gem-set Piaget Sautoir watch.

Watches of Switzerland’s Knightsbridge store. About half of the retailer’s business comes from supply-limited brands such as Rolex and Patek Philippe, and it uses AI to decide what else goes in its windows.

In a recent development, stock availability is a top priority for clients. What do you do to ensure your stores have the right products?

About half of our business relies on brands such as Rolex and Patek Philippe, which have limited supply and are sold to customers who have waited patiently. But we use artificial intelligence tools to identify trends. For example, when customers browse our watches online, our tool ignores the brand and detects specific watch attributes, such as case size, price point, and strap material; these criteria help us adjust our stock accordingly.

How do you turn digital activity into a commercial opportunity?

Unlike other apparel items, watches can be appreciated even more online, as we can show minute details that are not visible to the naked eye, and we can even show the movement, the beating heart of a timepiece, which is often hidden. We, of course, offer online chats with experts, and one of our points of difference is that we own Hodinkee, the most trusted online watch magazine, with shopping links to our website.

Women are becoming more key for the watch industry; how are you supporting this growth?

Our new store in Glasgow is a good example: the team there is led by a woman, and the salesforce is evenly split 50-50 between men and women. We also have three watchmakers in residence to service timepieces: one man and two women.

Sources indicate that the Vogue Business consumer sentiment ranking assesses brands based on consumers’ opinions and willingness to buy. The criteria analyzed range from basic brand awareness to brand loyalty and purchase intent. Brands are also evaluated on perceived quality, with survey participants answering questions about customer service, in-store experience, design, and sustainability, among others. Respondents have also appraised a brand’s storytelling, role in society, perceived timelessness, digital content, trust, and sense of style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Journalists who’ve been anxious about losing their jobs to artificial intelligence would be wise to focus on a different, altogether less menacing but equally impressive threat: 14-year-old Eli Goldfine, the shoestring podcaster from Westchester County who last week conducted a 90-minute interview with Sam Bankman-Fried, who’s currently serving a 25-year sentence in federal prison for orchestrating a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency grift.

Recent findings suggest that so how, exactly, does this precocious ninth grader with braces—and not a reporter from one of the scores of legacy publications who’d surely be gunning for access to the disgraced cryptocurrency king—score an interview so coveted? “I had written about Sam on Twitter a little bit, and it got picked up by the person who was at the time running Sam’s account,” Goldfine, who hosts a podcast about prediction markets called The Supercycle, told me earlier this week. “I think they were impressed with my knowledge of various parts of his criminal case.”.

In a recent development, goldfine’s classmates are impressed, too, even though he’s been on the receiving end of some gentle ribbing about his on-air ad reads. But can any of them say they got Bankman-Fried to speculate on the likelihood that AI will bring about the extinction of the human race? ("Less than 50%, more than 10%," by the way). Before school’s out for Thanksgiving break, Goldfine joined GQ to talk about his media diet, dream interview subject, and the mechanics of interviewing a man behind bars.

Recent findings suggest that eli Goldfine: Wait, just to step back here. Are you printing what I'm going to say, or is this just for you to know? It's not a video on the site, right?

Okay. So my podcast is primarily about prediction markets and other broader markets. And I got into that during the 2024 election. My dad showed me Polymarket and I thought, "Wow, this is really cool. It's people staking money on different sides of an outcome. And when you put all that price signal together, it converges on a really accurate probability of a given event happening. How could I investigate this more?" So I learned more about it and I started trading on a fake-money version of Polymarket.

It's called Manifold Markets. And what's cool about that one is, anyone can create their own question rather than the platform deciding. And anyway, I got really into it and then I was like, “I'll write a couple articles about this because I have some ideas.” And then I started doing interviews and it all kind of came out from that.

So does that serve such an vital function? Probably not. And it's fair to say the same about prediction markets on sports. Does anyone really need to know the outcome of a sports game that badly? Latest Update: K-Pop Stars, Art and Unexpected Collabs: Inside the 2026 Watch Innovation Playbook
