💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that after a tough 2025 for the watch industry, 2026 has painted a sunnier picture.
  • Nevertheless, after the shock of the annus horribilis that was 2025, most brands have reviewed their investments, typically ditching high-cost, high-visibility sponsorships in favor of projects that deliver more immediate, tangible results.
  • Following in the footsteps of Rolex, which left Formula 1 sponsorship to LVMH-owned brands, Hublot reduced its involvement in soccer to strengthen collaborations with artists and existing ambassadors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after a tough 2025 for the watch industry, 2026 has painted a sunnier picture. Overall export value has grown by 2.7% thanks to unexpected pockets of growth in emerging markets (India +28.5%, Thailand +8.6%, and Mexico +6.2%), which offset drops in traditionally strong markets like China (-5.9%) and Saudi Arabia (-10.3%).

Nevertheless, after the shock of the annus horribilis that was 2025, most brands have reviewed their investments, typically ditching high-cost, high-visibility sponsorships in favor of projects that deliver more immediate, tangible results.

Following in the footsteps of Rolex, which left Formula 1 sponsorship to LVMH-owned brands, Hublot reduced its involvement in soccer to strengthen collaborations with artists and existing ambassadors. Ambassadorship became an evolving concept this year, with brands moving beyond campaign appearances to involve their ambassadors in creating the timepieces they promote: Audemars Piguet released a watch co-designed with tennis player Serena Williams, Movado teamed up with American rapper Ludacris, and Hublot unveiled a watch by British designer Samuel Ross. Another defining ambassador trend has been the emergence of partnerships with non-Western talents predominantly from South Korea, Thailand and India, countries that are delivering positive results for the watch business.

It has been revealed that brands have also been experimenting with collaboration projects outside the typical realms of sports and cars. Visual art has emerged as the watchmakers’ upcoming playground, with Vacheron Constantin unveiling its first mentorship project with The Met in New York and Piaget releasing another watch made in collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation. But there were also some unexpected twists, notably with Roger Dubuis teaming up with tattoo artist Dr Woo and Hublot partnering with artist Jeff Koons for timepieces.

Hublot’s partnership with artist Jeff Koons.

According to recent reports, brands also ventured into upcoming partnerships. Richard Mille teamed up with the Italian high-end bicycle manufacturer Colnago, Zenith partnered with furniture maker USM, while Ulysse Nardin established an innovative tie-up with pastry chef Amaury Guichon for its Unstoppable Spirits campaign. This suggests that engagement with the luxury watch category is also operating as a gateway to more niche cultural and lifestyle pursuits.

In a recent development, but collaborations between watch brands were the most prominent modus operandi of 2026. Audemars Piguet and Swatch took center stage with their Royal Pop collection, while Louis Vuitton partnered with independent watchmaker De Bethune and Ulysse Nardin joined forces with Urwerk to unveil the UR-Freak, one of the most contemporary iterations of luxury watchmaking in recent times.

Consumers reflected these sentiments in our 2026 survey. When asked, “Which developments excite you the most in the luxury watch market?”, the top three answers were: limited-edition watches, resale service and experiences. Excitement around resale services was consistent across age groups, with a median value of 60% — the lowest recorded value was among Gen Z (18-24) at 56.4% and the highest among boomers (55-64) at 65.5%.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, 70% of luxury watch consumers globally are excited about limited-edition watches, with this rising to 76% among Chinese shoppers. When it comes to experiences, 58% globally are most excited about these novel ways to experience brands, especially 25- to 34-year-olds, at 66%.

Sources indicate that longines has risen to the top 10 in the Vogue Business Watch Index this year (seeing a 58% increase), thanks to a combination of niche sports and celebrity tie-ins. The brand’s performance was helped by its long-time partnerships with equestrian competitions, which this year enjoyed extra visibility through the digital game Longines League of Nations™ Memory Game, developed in partnership with Fédération Équestre Internationale (FEI). The Commonwealth Games, which take place every four years and of which Longines was a sponsor, offered another boost. Longines’s astute partnerships are also noteworthy. Alongside its long-standing relationships with Jennifer Lawrence and Kate Winslet, the brand has partnered with rising Thai talent, gaining visibility in a country where Swiss watches have grown by 8.6% in value between January and September 2026 vs the same period in 2025.

Meanwhile, “Wes Anderson: The Archives”, the exhibition held at the Design Museum in London between November 2025 and July 2026 and dedicated to the filmmaker and long-time ambassador, was one of the factors that helped Hamburg-headquartered Montblanc improve its innovation score. Another factor was the #LetsWrite campaign, which transformed some of Montblanc’s flagship stores worldwide into oases to rediscover the art of writing. The visibility of these novel initiatives propelled the brand to sixth place, up 36 percentage points.

Montblanc’s partnership with long-time ambassador Wes Anderson, celebrated in the Design Museum’s “Wes Anderson: The Archives” exhibition, helped the brand climb to sixth place for innovation.

Panerai and Piaget both grew by 16%, earning their positions in the top 10. Panerai’s brand exhibition in its hometown of Florence boosted the brand’s score, along with customer services such as virtual try-ons. The collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation, an innovative use of a Snapchat lens for virtual try-on, and the offer of a digital product passport (DPP) are some of the factors behind Piaget’s progress.

At the top of the table, despite a few shuffles, last year’s best performers broadly maintained their positions this year. Breitling takes the crown with 11 percentage points of growth, jumping two positions ahead of IWC and Cartier, which in 2026 occupied second and third place, respectively. Chopard sits in fourth alongside Panerai, which records a substantial 16% increase in fifth position, up three positions vs. 2025. Hublot slips to sixth, down from fourth last year.

In a recent development, more shifts have happened at the bottom of the table. Although Patek Philippe and Tudor remain among the bottom five, Zenith marks a standout recovery with an increase of 26 percentage points, alongside Rolex, which has moved up by 10 percentage points.

Sources indicate that both Movado and A. Lange & Söhne have lost about 10 percentage points, moving down among the bottom 10 brands, alongside Omega, which has fallen 20 percentage points and landed in the bottom five. Despite its collaboration with Swatch for the Audemars Piguet x Swatch Royal Pop Collection, the Le Brassus-headquartered brand dropped 26 percentage points, losing five positions and landing in the middle of the table at 11th place.

It has been revealed that seismic shifts in the watch industry have prompted brands to sign a newly introduced cohort of celebrity ambassadors who can seduce audiences in promising new markets. While China’s economic landscape still keeps imports in negative territory, and the war in Iran has disrupted the Middle East market, with Saudi Arabia’s market contracting by 10.3%, India, South Korea and Thailand are growing.

In a recent development, in June 2026, Rolex grabbed headlines not with one of its many leading tennis players at Roland-Garros but with the appointment of Priyanka Chopra Jones as its first Indian entertainment celebrity to join its roster of “testimonees” — the brand’s lingo for ambassadors. The brand had previously signed only Indian athletes, including tennis player Vijay Amritraj and golfers Jeev Milkha Singh and Anirban Lahiri. This move acknowledges the growing importance of the Indian market in the watchmaking business. According to the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry, the value of Indian imports of timepieces grew by 28.5% in 2026 vs 2025 (January–September) and by 40.9% vs 2024 (January–September).

Other watch brands have also signed up Indian celebrities: Omega appointed javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, and Rado teamed up with female cricketer Smriti Mandhana.

Recent findings suggest that in the wake of Thailand’s rise in the watch business, brands have been signing up Thai talents in rapid succession. This summer, Cartier added actor PP Krit Amnuaydechkorn to its portfolio of Thai ambassadors, which already includes singer and actor Jeff Satur, actress Kimberley Anne Woltemas, and actor Tor Thanapob Leeratanakachorn. Meanwhile, Piaget has teamed up with Thai actor Apo Nattawin Wattanagitiphat since 2024, and Casio featured Thai kickboxing world champion Superbon Singha Mawynn in its “Tough Like You” campaign.

It has been revealed that but a top priority for watch brands right now is having a South Korean talent, preferably from one of the bands riding high on K-pop mania. At the start of 2026, Hublot signed Jung Kook, a member of the beloved band BTS, who has over 27 million Instagram followers and 35 million on TikTok. Meanwhile, in 2025, Piaget appointed actress Gianna Jun, following in the footsteps of Longines, which the year before brought on board actress Bae Suzy, a former member of the K-pop girl group Miss A. Omega has three South Korean ambassadors: actress Shin Min-a and actors Park Bo-gum and Hyun Bin, while Chopard signed all four members of K-pop band Aespa — Karina, Winter, Giselle and Ningning — back in 2023.

Hublot signed Jung Kook, a member of the beloved band BTS, who has over 27 million Instagram followers and 35 million on TikTok.

Watchmakers have also experimented with a different cohort of ambassadors: Ulysse Nardin’s tie-up with chef chocolatier Amaury Guichon led to approximately half a billion views across social media, according to the brand, while Gallet, a brand owned by Breitling, has partnered with a group of six explorers active on social media for its relaunch campaign.

Sources indicate that the watch and automotive partnership is nothing new, thanks to the overlapping interests in mechanics, design and a predominantly male clientele, and recent collaborations suggest this is unlikely to change. Tag Heuer’s long-standing partnership with Formula 1 was boosted last year when LVMH took over the tournament sponsorship from Rolex, offering the brand the opportunity to further expand associated products and storytelling. Early this year, Breitling signed a global, multi-year partnership with Aston Martin, leading to the release of the Navitimer B01 Chronograph 43 Aston Martin Aramco, marking Breitling’s return to Formula 1. Bianchet revealed a partnership with Maserati, unveiling the first UltraFino Maserati at Watches and Wonders in Geneva. Meanwhile, Casio teamed up with Toyota Racing, and Roger Dubuis confirmed its enduring association with Lamborghini.

Recent findings suggest that but there have been some twists in the category. At the end of the summer, Seiko announced a collaboration with Honda — not with any of its cars or muscular motorcycles, but with Motocompo, a compact, foldable scooter — the very opposite of a bling, power-signaling motor vehicle. It was one of many recent unusual collaborations that watchmakers hope will reach upcoming audiences, unveil novel features of their brand’s DNA, and make them seem less intimidating and more approachable.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of 2025, Zenith collaborated with the furniture firm USM, whose designs are ubiquitous at Zenith’s headquarters in Le Locle, on a series of four Defy watches featuring USM’s saturated colors and delivered in USM boxes made with its signature Haller modular system. Rado entered into a similar partnership with the industrial design company Tej Chauhan.

According to recent reports, more unusual still, in September this year, Casio unveiled a new AQ-230ECK with a distinctive matcha-tea-green dial featuring a black fox at 12 o’clock and, at 6 o’clock, the logo of Café Kitsuné, the coffee shop chain of French-Japanese brand Maison Kitsuné. This shows the trend toward unlikely collaborators extends beyond the luxury end of the market and is taking root across the sector as a whole.

In a recent development, another unlikely partnership was between German watchmaker Nomos and Doctors Without Borders, which aims to raise funds and awareness for the work of doctors in areas plagued by wars, natural disasters and epidemics, and to provide access to necessary health care. This partnership resulted in a limited-edition Ludwig model featuring a red number 12 on a white dial.

Industry observers note that even tried-and-tested art partnerships have lately taken on unexpected forms. At the end of last year, Roger Dubuis released a series of watches in collaboration with Los Angeles-based tattoo artist Dr Woo, while this year, Vacheron Constantin invited artists such as glass-makers and wood furniture designers to miniaturize their work to fit the proportions of a watch dial.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Hublot grabbed headlines with two new watches co-designed by artist Jeff Koons. The first is the Hublot Classic Fusion Balloon Dog, a series of three timepieces in red, blue and silver, each limited to 200 pieces, mimicking Koons’s iconic inflated dog sculpture in its rounded bezel, case and crown. The second is the more elaborate, gem-set Hublot MP-14 Origin inspired by Koons’s Gazing Ball works. In some ways, these standout partnerships make the high-profile, long-established relationship between Omega and the James Bond franchise — most recently leading to six new Seamaster Diver models inspired by James Bond and Spectre — seem quite tame in comparison.

It has been revealed that omega’s fresh Seamaster Diver 300M Spectre edition. Released on Global James Bond Day, it’s the first time in the brand’s three-decade partnership with the franchise that Omega has made a watch for Bond’s nemesis.

During the watch fair Watches and Wonders in April, Swatch ran a newspaper ad that read, “The real wonders are happening in May.” What subsequently happened was the collaboration that dominated the news in 2026: the one between Audemars Piguet and Swatch for the release of the Royal Pop, the $439 pocket watch shaped like Audemars Piguet’s Royal Oak, made in the eye-popping colors and affordable materials of a Swatch timepiece.

In a recent development, it marks the first time Swatch collaborated with a brand outside its portfolio, as previous tie-ups were with Omega for the MoonSwatch and Blancpain for Fifty Fathoms. It’s also the very first time Audemars Piguet released a watch bearing its logo and costing considerably less than $20,000, its usual entry price.

The enthusiasm around the watch release was so exceptionally high that it led to people camping outside the authorized Swatch stores for days, marred by episodes of violence. “Everybody was so enthusiastic about this innovative product and the combination of two iconic Swiss brands in extremely opposite segments that they forgot the Royal Pop is not a product to be sold only on the launch day but over many months,” Swatch CEO Nick Hayek said, answering the criticism around the launch in an interview with Vogue Business.

It has been revealed that but the collaboration was still significant because it considerably boosted awareness of both brands and increased traffic to both their websites and social media accounts. Mr Hayek also hopes that the collaboration can reignite interest in more affordable watches in a climate where the industry keeps moving upmarket. “My father always said: be careful when an industry keeps moving further upmarket and becoming more expensive — you lose creativity, you lose innovation,” Hayek claims. “It’s the same in many industries. If a luxury industry starts producing only for the elite, only for a small bubble of people, eventually billions of real people disconnect.”.

Industry observers note that double-signed watches have been a feature of the watch industry since its infancy, when a watch would bear the logo of the movement maker as well as that of the retailer. In the vintage market, double-signed timepieces such as Audemars Piguet-Tiffany or Patek Philippe-Cartier are sought-after rarities. But as watchmakers progressively chose to produce their own movements, double-signed watches disappeared. This latest wave of watch brand collaborations aims not only to blend design and storytelling to appeal to a much wider audience, but also to combine elements of the brands’ own movements to intrigue watch nerds.

What have you done to bring your brand closer to women?

Sources indicate that we believe our roots in technique and our passion for precision are genderless and can appeal to both men and women. Women have always been part of the brand’s history, as the jewelry watches in our archive prove. We have never wanted to create a separate universe and products specifically for women. Instead, we have worked on our products, the design of our boutiques, and our communications.

Industry observers note that we have expanded our product range to include more ergonomic case sizes, giving clients the freedom to choose proportions that best suit their wrists and personal style. We have also focused on making our boutique design aesthetically appealing and welcoming for both men and women. And finally, communication has been crucial. Female ambassadors, such as supermodel Gisele Bündchen and Eileen Gu, have also hugely helped raise our brand awareness among women.

IWC ambassador Gisele Bündchen.

How has your loyalty to Formula 1 played out in your strategy?

Formula 1, and motorsport in general, has always been part of our identity, and we continue to show that loyalty through our ambassadors, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. Our affinity for Formula 1 led to last year’s collaboration with F1 The Movie.

Industry observers note that our loyalty to Formula 1 is also helping the brand raise its profile among women. In the past, the Formula 1 audience was 80% men and only 20% women. The balance is now 50-50, meaning more women have grown closer to our brand thanks to Formula 1. A case in point is our new friend of the brand, George Russell’s fiancée, Carmen Montero Mundt, who spontaneously began wearing our brand. It often happens that our clients’ wives also like the brand, and entire generations often become loyal clients.

How have you employed social media to draw women closer?

Our social media channels help us connect with women. On our channels, we regularly show famous women and models wearing our watches, as well as the women working in our manufacture. Last year, we launched the series “IWC.Inspired”, which celebrates the achievements of women from all walks of life who use time wisely and with purpose. So far, we have featured skincare expert Melanie Grant, Michelle Kennedy, founder of the social networking app Peanut, and British model and entrepreneur Jodie Kidd.

The Vogue Business Watch Index assigns an innovation score to the experiences and services brands offer to existing clients, prospective ones and stakeholders at large across the digital and physical worlds.

The services examined in the digital world include NFTs, augmented reality and virtual reality on brands’ websites and social media channels that allow virtual try-ons or immersive, game-like experiences; collaborations across films, TV and gaming; and the digital translation of physical experiences such as exhibitions.

Among the services assessed in the physical world are traceability tools, resale services offered either directly by the brand or a third party, the acceptance of cryptocurrency payments, and virtual consultations straddling the digital and physical realms.

According to recent reports, consumer research was conducted over October 2026, while digital data and innovation audit data captured the period between September 2025 and August 2026. Data was captured across 20 brands and metrics are weighted according to the importance assigned by survey respondents.

Popeyes Beat KFC In My Chicken Sandwich Showdown—But Can It Take Down Chick-fil-A?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few fast food rivalries are as competitive as the battle for the best chicken sandwich.
  • In my previous chicken sandwich showdown, I put KFC and Popeyes head-to-head to see which chain served the better sandwich.
  • Chick-fil-A has built its reputation around a simple, flavorful chicken sandwich that doesn’t need much to stand out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few fast food rivalries are as competitive as the battle for the best chicken sandwich. And while plenty of chains have introduced their own versions over the years, Chick-fil-A and Popeyes remain two of the biggest names in the conversation.

In my previous chicken sandwich showdown, I put KFC and Popeyes head-to-head to see which chain served the better sandwich. Popeyes ultimately came out on top, thanks to its bold seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings. This time, I’m putting Popeyes up against one of its biggest competitors: Chick-fil-A.

Chick-fil-A has built its reputation around a simple, flavorful chicken sandwich that doesn’t need much to stand out. Popeyes, meanwhile, practically broke the internet when it introduced its now-famous chicken sandwich in 2019, sparking a fast food frenzy.

Sources indicate that I ordered each chain’s original chicken sandwich to compare flavor, texture, juiciness, and overall balance. Both have their strengths, but only one can move on as my favorite.

Chick-fil-A’s Original Chicken Sandwich keeps things simple with a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, and a toasted bun.

In a recent development, chick-fil-A’s chicken is so recognizable for a reason. The seasoning and brine give the fillet a savory, slightly tangy flavor that’s hard to beat, while the crispy breading contrasts nicely with the juicy chicken. The pickles also do their job, adding just enough acidity and crunch to balance out the richness.

My biggest complaint is that I wanted a little more from the sandwich. Compared to other fast food chicken sandwiches I’ve tried, many of which come with some type of sauce, Chick-fil-A’s original feels a bit plain. The chicken has enough flavor to stand on its own, but I think a little mayo or another sauce would have made the overall sandwich even better.

Still, there’s something to be stated for a chicken sandwich that relies almost entirely on the quality and flavor of the chicken itself.

Popeyes’ Classic Chicken Sandwich features a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, mayo, and a toasted brioche bun. The sandwich that practically broke the internet when it released in 2019 still lives up to the hype.

I’ve had this sandwich before where the chicken was slightly dry in spots, but thankfully that wasn’t the case this time. The fillet was juicy, flavorful, and incredibly well-seasoned. The breading had a satisfying crunch, and the bold, savory flavor made me want to keep going back for another bite.

Recent findings suggest that the mayo was another important part of the sandwich, adding a tangy creaminess that complemented the chicken without overpowering it. Paired with the crisp pickles, it helped balance out the richness of the fried fillet.

In a recent development, I also really appreciated the proportions. The soft brioche bun held everything together without overwhelming the chicken, and each bite had a good balance of meat, breading, sauce, and pickles.

It has been revealed that while Popeyes might not always deliver the most consistently juicy chicken, everything came together particularly well during this taste test. Between the seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings, it’s easy to understand why this sandwich became such a phenomenon in the first place.

Popeyes already managed to beat KFC in my previous comparison, and after going up against Chick-fil-A, it’s keeping its winning streak alive.

It has been revealed that chick-fil-A arguably has the more distinctive chicken flavor, thanks to its savory, slightly tangy seasoning. But when I’m ordering a chicken sandwich, I want the entire thing to work together, and that’s where Popeyes has the advantage.

In a recent development, chick-fil-A is still a great option, especially if you prefer a simpler sandwich that lets the chicken do most of the work. But after trying both, Popeyes delivered the better overall experience. With two wins under its belt, Popeyes is proving to be a pretty tough sandwich to beat.

  • Industry observers note that tripp explained that her oysters, cultivated in the cold tidal waters of the Lower Weskeag River, take three years to reach maturity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Attendees of Bon Appétit Live experienced a taste of Maine through a hands-on lobster cooking class and a demonstration of wild blueberry cornmeal shortcakes, both hosted by Visit Maine.

Industry observers note that the class, Lobster 101, was led by Bon Appétit manager of audience strategy Carly Westerfield and Krista Tripp, founder of Aphrodite Oysters in South Thomaston, Maine. Attendees learned how to break down a whole, steamed two-pound Maine lobster and transform the meat into a rich, creamy lobster dip—ideal for holiday hosting. Guests then enjoyed the fruits of their labor, sampling the freshly made dip with Ritz crackers before tasting oysters.

Industry observers note that tripp explained that her oysters, cultivated in the cold tidal waters of the Lower Weskeag River, take three years to reach maturity. Known for their distinctive fluted shells, they offer a briny, mineral-rich flavor balanced by a mellow sweetness.

Recent findings suggest that after years as a lobster harvester, Tripp started Aphrodite Oysters to diversify her lobster business and has since shifted her focus to oyster cultivation full-time. She’s come to appreciate the many environmental benefits of farming and consuming them. Her oysters filter up to 50 gallons of water a day, taking in nitrogen and sequestering some for their growing shells. “Eating an oyster is contributing to the environment,” she declared. Indeed, water test scores have improved at her farm, demonstrating that bivalves help create a healthier ecosystem.

In a recent development, before the end of the class, a few brave attendees volunteered to shuck their first oysters. Krista guided them through the process, demonstrating how to safely do it at home by protecting the hand holding the shellfish with a towel and gently working the knife into the hinge until the shell released. The well-earned reward was another taste of the Penobscot Bay, as fresh and pristine as the waters themselves.

Later in the day, guests in the Demo Kitchen were treated to Cornmeal Shortcakes with Blueberry Compote, prepared by Bon Appétit senior Test Kitchen editor Jesse Szewczyk. The compote featured wild Maine blueberries from Brodis Blueberries, a multigenerational family farm in Hope, Maine, stewarded by Ron Howard and his family. Howard joined Szewczyk for the demo, where he shared that 99% of the wild blueberries grown and harvested in the United States come from Maine. Attendees learned that they have been growing since the end of the Ice Age, when the tenacious plants, fortified by ericoid mycorrhizal fungi, began to grow and colonize the newly exposed land as glaciers retreated. An crucial food source for Native Americans, wild blueberries were valued by Indigenous communities for their nutritional benefits well before the modern superfood movement.

Speaking passionately, Howard discussed the many challenges facing Maine growers, including tariffs and currency exchange fluctuations, particularly the impact of a stronger Canadian dollar. Like many Maine farmers, the family has had to get creative. Howard invested in latest equipment, including a more efficient type of harvester that allowed the business to scale up and sell to retailers. They created a shelf-stable, freeze-dried product with no added ingredients, allowing them to ship their product beyond the local area. Howard and his son started a distillery, where they use wild blueberries to make an eau de vie and vodka. They have also begun hosting a Wild Blueberry Weekend, opening the doors to the farm and educating the public about the unique benefits of their crop and their growing process.

Carolann Ouellette, director of the Maine Office of Tourism, emphasized that visiting Maine and engaging with local growers and producers such as Howard and Tripp was the best way to experience the state’s diverse bounty. “The relationship between people and nature is inseparable, and stewardship is an vital part of the state's identity,” she reflected. Ouellette grew up in Newly introduced Jersey but relocated to Maine over 40 years ago. Her family used to visit Maine when she was a child, and she recalls those experiences vividly: “As a kid, I remember, when you get to Maine, you can smell the pine and spruce.” It’s those potent memories that drew her to the state permanently, a place she described as “filled with hardworking, welcoming communities that depend on one another.”.

A few years ago, Visit Maine began placing greater emphasis on the state’s culinary identity. Ouellette remarked that awareness of Maine as a food destination continues to grow, “Sea to table with local ingredients is what we were doing before it was a thing.” Beyond the lobster, Visit Maine has been intentional about showcasing the breadth of the state’s agricultural, fishing, and heritage industries. Apples, potatoes, kelp, seaweed, and grains are just a few of the local ingredients featured in Visit Maine’s newsletter and Bountiful Plate video series, which highlights food and beverage producers throughout the state. Ouellette noted that Maine’s food culture is more diverse than many people expect, and its abundance of local products has attracted an interesting mix of exceptional chefs, many of whom are deeply embedded in their communities. Ouellette cited Tripp’s practice of personally delivering her oysters to local restaurants as an example of how the hospitality ecosystem is interconnected.

Most crucial, Ouellette emphasized that sustainability and stewardship are central to the state’s approach to its food systems and relationship with the landscape. “You can’t get much fresher than food in Maine,” she concluded.

Bon Appétit LIVE 2026 was sponsored by East Fork, Visit Maine, and S.Pellegrino® Sparkling Natural Mineral Water with thanks to All-Clad, As Ever, Bachan’s, Better Sour, Field Tech giant, Floura, Gimme Seaweed, GOODLES, Graza, Hedley & Bennett, Kann Coffee, Material Kitchen, Misen, Owala®, Rip Van, SharkNinja, and Staub.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

According to recent reports, mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

In a recent development, set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Recent findings suggest that transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

In a recent development, bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

It has been revealed that do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following a challenging 2025, 2026 has offered some green shoots for the luxury watch industry.
  • Overall Swiss export value has grown by 2.7%, driven by unexpected pockets of growth in emerging markets (India +28.5%, Thailand +8.6% and Mexico +6.2%), which offset drops in traditionally strong markets like China (-5.9%) and Saudi Arabia (-10.3%).
  • Sources indicate that the digital audit highlights how brands are appointing high-profile cultural influencers in newer markets, from K-pop stars to Thai actors, as brand ambassadors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a challenging 2025, 2026 has offered some green shoots for the luxury watch industry.

Overall Swiss export value has grown by 2.7%, driven by unexpected pockets of growth in emerging markets (India +28.5%, Thailand +8.6% and Mexico +6.2%), which offset drops in traditionally strong markets like China (-5.9%) and Saudi Arabia (-10.3%). The latest consumer research from Vogue Business highlights nuanced market trends, underscoring the need for watch brands to pay particular attention to local cultural needs. In China, for example, despite a broader market slowdown, 55% of luxury watch consumers surveyed have bought themselves a timepiece to celebrate their birthday. Recognizing these behaviors can help brands make their messaging more impactful — a strategy that will become increasingly notable as shoppers rely more on emerging channels to discover products and brands.

Sources indicate that the digital audit highlights how brands are appointing high-profile cultural influencers in newer markets, from K-pop stars to Thai actors, as brand ambassadors. As the geography of growth shifts, so too must campaign strategies.

Sources indicate that and while mainstream sports like motoring and equestrianism have historically provided key partnerships for luxury watches, more niche sports are helping brands reach latest audiences. Yet our digital analysis also exposes some tensions the industry is grappling with; the channels relied on for sourcing trusted information are not always the channels consumers use to discover new brands and products and, as use of generative AI becomes more widespread, brands will need to adapt their digital strategies to boost visibility in this emerging space. Opportunities also remain to strengthen the omnichannel experience, with our survey highlighting shopper frustration over limited online service options.

Recent findings suggest that in a market steeped in tradition, established leaders have defended their positions in the ranking, while collaborations with the worlds of film and art are helping legacy brands stay fresh. Consumers also continue to favor buying directly from brands, with 47.8% on average having bought their most recent watches this way or from multibrand specialists (22.5% on average). Yet while brand awareness has risen year on year, purchase intent remains relatively flat, even as enthusiasm for resale grows. As much as the availability of digital product passports (DPPs) and authentication services may encourage shoppers to engage with resale platforms, economic pressures expose a bigger driver: price sensitivity. Older consumers are particularly likely to wait for sales and discounts before making a purchase. This suggests that the demand for innovation in the pre-loved watch environment is as much a reflection of price sensitivity as it is the result of improved services in this space. It also means that, over the coming year, luxury watch brands will need to work harder to defend those “brand new” watch sales in the primary market.

Recent findings suggest that cartier retains its leadership position for the third year. This summer, Cartier added actor PP Krit Amnuaydechkorn to its portfolio of Thai ambassadors, which already includes singer and actor Jeff Satur, actress Kimberley Anne Woltemas and actor Tor Thanapob Leeratanakachorn. This has helped it to maintain momentum on platforms like Instagram and gain ground on TikTok. Yet while awareness has risen, consumer opinion is more mixed, with small declines in perception of innovation, value for money and experience, showing even leaders cannot rest on their laurels.

It has been revealed that improved consumer perception, the highest recognition and highest purchase intent have helped Rolex to secure the second spot in this year’s ranking. The availability of certified pre-owned Rolexes at official stockists means the brand is well-positioned to take advantage of the rising demand for pre-loved luxury timepieces. Small but steady gains on all Western social media platforms have also helped the brand to stay front of mind for consumers in a cluttered digital landscape.

In a recent development, omega narrowly misses out on second place this year. The brand benefits from high awareness and improved perception across several metrics. Its strong digital performance is helped by high-profile collaborations, for example, its James Bond/Spectre partnerships, but the provision of omnichannel features and innovation performance leave room for growth.

After breaking into the top five last year, Tag Heuer has managed to hold on to fourth position. The brand benefits from significant gains in consumer awareness, perception of quality, and positive association with more emotional drivers, as well as increased purchase intent in a market where this is relatively flat. Against a backdrop of rising price sensitivity, its positioning may help it to weather a volatile economic period.

According to recent reports, after two years spent in sixth position, IWC moves into the top five for the first time this year. The brand ranks second for both Digital and Innovation, with a focused strategy on social media helping it reach latest audiences. Its ongoing partnership with F1 is also helping to recruit more female followers, while its IWC.Inspired series celebrates women from all walks of life. Meanwhile, its partnership with Watchfinder enables consumers to part-exchange pre-loved IWC timepieces when making their next purchase, providing a seamless way to engage with the increasingly relevant resale market.

Twenty brands are assessed for the Vogue Business Watch Index, with brand performance evaluated against over 100 data points spanning consumer sentiment, digital marketing and innovation.

Sources indicate that the weightings of each assessment category and their metrics are determined by industry relevance and importance to the consumer, allowing for an objective assessment of a brand’s performance. The final weighting for each category is agreed upon following a review process with our data analysts and expert editors. This year, we removed Chinese platforms from our digital audit due to lack of data availability, with weightings being reassigned proportionally to retained digital platforms (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Google Search).

Consumer research remains fundamental to the Vogue Business Watch Index, with readers across several Condé Nast titles — including Vogue, GQ, Vanity Fair and Condé Nast Traveler — participating in an annual consumer sentiment survey that ensures granularity is achieved when it comes to understanding awareness, customer challenges and brand perception. This year, we surveyed 1,020 qualified luxury watch consumers in seven markets (the US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Middle East and China). Among them, 60% of luxury watch consumers spent between €1,500 and €4,999 on luxury watches in the last five years, while 40% spent over €5,000.

Future iterations of the Vogue Business Watch Index will continue to maximize the brands, metrics, and digital platforms assessed, with additions prioritized in line with industry needs and developments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that inspired by the iconic egg and sausage sandwich on a pancake bun, this breakfast casserole is cheesy and just a smidge sweet from the brushing of maple butter at the very end. Destined for holiday brunch tables everywhere and best enjoyed while you’re still in pajamas, this cozy bake will feed a full house. (Don’t be surprised if you find yourself making it again long after the last guest leaves though!).

More high-protein breakfast recipes here.

It has been revealed that place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Lightly coat a 13x9" baking dish with nonstick vegetable oil spray. Whisk 2½ cups (313 g) all-purpose flour, ¼ cup (50 g) sugar, 2 Tbsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine. Set aside.

Cook 2 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed, in a large skillet set over medium-high heat, stirring and breaking into small pieces with a wooden spoon, until browned and cooked through, 10–12 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer sausage to a small plate, leaving fat behind. Pour fat into a heatproof measuring glass. You want ½ cup fat; spoon out any excess or pour in vegetable oil as needed if you don’t have enough. Stir 2 large eggs and 2 cups whole milk into fat. Let sausage cool slightly, then crumble into small, even pieces with your hands.

Pour fat mixture into reserved dry ingredients and stir until just combined and no large dry pockets of flour remain (batter may be thin and lumpy; it’ll be fine). Set aside ½ cup sausage and ½ cup cheese from 8 oz. sharp yellow cheddar, coarsely grated (about 2 cups), for topping, then add remaining sausage and cheddar to batter and stirring until evenly distributed.

Sources indicate that scrape batter into prepared baking dish and evenly scatter reserved sausage and cheese over. Bake casserole until top springs back when gently pressed with your finger and a tester inserted into the center comes out with just a few moist crumbs attached, 20–30 minutes.

According to recent reports, just before casserole is done, heat 2 Tbsp. pure maple syrup and 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a small skillet over medium, stirring occasionally, until butter is melted, about 2 minutes.

It has been revealed that brush maple butter over casserole and let cool 10 minutes. Cut into squares. Serve with more maple syrup and butter alongside.

The real star here is the orzo. Toasted in butter until it’s deeply golden and nutty-fragrant, the pasta takes on a new personality. Unlike plain noodles, which quickly go limp in hot soup, well-toasted orzo stays al dente for longer, holding its shape and texture until you’ve doled out every bowl.

Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.

Sources indicate that season 1¼ lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs (4–5) all over with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Recent findings suggest that heat 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add 1 tsp. crushed fennel seeds, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. ground cardamom, and ¼ tsp. ground cloves and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 20 seconds. Add chicken, one 1" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or chicken stock, and 3 cups water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Partially cover pot, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part of a thigh registers at least 165°, 15–18 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Reduce heat to low and cover pot. Using 2 forks, shred chicken.

It has been revealed that melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and cook, stirring often, until golden brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Recent findings suggest that scrape orzo mixture into pot with broth. Increase heat to medium and simmer broth, uncovered, until orzo is just al dente, 8–10 minutes. Remove soup from heat and add shredded chicken, 5 oz. baby kale or spinach, and 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice. Stir until greens are just wilted. Taste and season with more salt if needed.

Breaking: The Tucson Restaurant Turning Cactus Into Fine Dining

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that traipsing through Tucson Mountain Park, a Midwestern blow-in might not identify much to eat.
  • Gray, tangled brittlebush, which the average Tucsonan walks or drives by almost daily, can be pressure-cooked, caramelized until black, and baked into cake.
  • Don’t even get Lopez started on the dozens of cacti varieties that thrive here, which the restaurant sources from local grower Toadlet Farm and which Lopez harvests throughout the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that traipsing through Tucson Mountain Park, a Midwestern blow-in might not identify much to eat. Plants armed with burs, barbs, and spines all but scream “do not touch.” For chef Aaron Lopez and June Chee, however, this prickly, dusty landscape stocks a pantry of possibility. The married co-owners of Ursa see the Arizona desert as a rich ground for foraging.

Gray, tangled brittlebush, which the average Tucsonan walks or drives by almost daily, can be pressure-cooked, caramelized until black, and baked into cake. Dusty, sage-colored salt bush, when hung to dry, takes on an intensely umami, aquatic saltiness like seaweed. The sweet buds of the Seussian-green palo verde tree become briny, like olives, when suffused with lye.

Don’t even get Lopez started on the dozens of cacti varieties that thrive here, which the restaurant sources from local grower Toadlet Farm and which Lopez harvests throughout the year. The restaurant processes the young and mature paddles, fruit and their seeds, buds, and flowers, which are then grilled, poached, cold-smoked, juiced, dehydrated, nixtamalized, or preserved into jam, wine, and vinegar.

There are hundreds of edible plants in the Sonoran Desert. Ursa strives to showcase their potential, one 10-course meal at a time.

“We treat Ursa as an art showroom, demonstrating to people what these plants can do, what sustainable means, and what was here before it got easy,” states Lopez. The idea was inspired in part by his Sonoran grandfather, Hector Lopez, who died in the spring. “He was the first person I ever heard say they’re proud to be from the desert,” the chef remarked.

Ursa began as a pop-up in California in 2023. Lopez and Chee moved to a historic brick building in downtown Tucson, re-opening their doors in October 2025. It’s a homecoming of sorts for the couple, who are both from the Sonoran Desert borderlands. They met in Hawaii, where Chee was working in clean energy and transportation. Lopez, meanwhile, spent roughly 18 years cooking in fine dining and modern progressive restaurants like Redbird and Orsa & Winston in LA, and Pai Honolulu. But he was longing for the desert.

Recent findings suggest that after helping a friend open a restaurant and hosting a few popups in Austin, Lopez and Chee bought a desert foraging guide, packed up their two dogs and began driving around the Southwest. It made sense to settle in Tucson, which was recognized by UNESCO in 2015 as a Creative City of Gastronomy for its continuous 4,000-year agricultural history and deeply rooted Sonoran Desert food traditions.

“That’s a unique thing about being here, the connection from seed to plant to restaurant that we hadn’t been able to grasp before,” Chee says.

In a recent development, consider a recent course that Ursa built around tepary beans, in which the ancient, nutty bean is refried and topped with h:al squash that’s been lactofermented. The squash’s leaves are fermented to make Japanese-style kosho and its flowers are pickled, dried, crushed with dried saltbush, then tossed with barrel cactus seeds for a desert furikake. It’s served with grilled coins of chorizo made from Lopez’s great-grandmother’s recipe and housemade flour tortillas, to all be washed down with an amazake drink made from fermented wheat and goat fat. Don’t get too attached, however. Riffs owing to finicky ingredient availability occur here almost daily.

Sources indicate that running a restaurant using only ingredients foraged and farmed from within about eight to 10 miles means abiding by pretty intense guardrails. The only wheat used is pima club, an ancient soft white variety cultivated for centuries by the Akimel O’odham (Pima) people. Ursa does not use cucumbers, radishes or citrus.

“We’re not trying to substitute anything, like, ‘How do we achieve cucumber? Let’s grab a cactus,’” Lopez says. “We have to throw everything out, really strip it down. Sometimes we have to let the ingredients be bitter or spicy. We have to put our egos aside and let the ingredient be the star.”.

For staff who didn’t grow up or learn to cook here, the learning curve at Ursa can feel a little like alighting on a new planet, even if certain flora happen to resemble prickly weeds in their own backyards.

It has been revealed that “We have these really cool moments in the restaurant where people are like, Oh! I have lamb’s quarter just growing in my yard!” Chee states of the spinach-like desert green that appears all over Ursa’s menu.

A young Aaron Lopez with his grandfather Hector Lopez.

Ursa’s approach isn’t always easy for customers to understand, so the couple came up with a more down-to-earth option. This fall, the restaurant debuted a four-course, family-style Lineage menu for $75, alongside the existing 10-course Harvest menu ($150). There’s now a pozole course inspired by the family’s annual springtime tradition of roasting goat in agave leaves, barbacoa-style, and shredding it for soup, and a red masa tamal with glazed quail and yucca blossoms in mole made with burnt mesquite bread, a technique Lopez remembers from childhood.

The idea took shape during Ursa’s extended summer break, as Lopez recovered from foot surgery and reflected on the loss of his late grandfather, the tenacious keeper of family traditions.

According to recent reports, “I feel so much closer to my ancestors and the land; we want Ursa to be less esoteric and more soulful,” he says. “The story of Ursa is partly of the desert, partly my family. Now we’ve advanced to the point where they’re symbiotic, and I can't tell them apart.”.

We Tried 6 Store-Bought Pumpkin Pies—These Are The Only 2 Worth Serving At Thanksgiving

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving.
  • According to recent reports, but sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch.
  • It primarily comes down to the crust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving. You need turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and, of course, a slice of pie to round out your meal. And pumpkin pie is the undeniable star of the dessert table.

According to recent reports, but sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch. So we tried six different grocery store pumpkin pies to find the best store-bought shortcut. And our team's verdict was pretty unanimous, even if it’s a bit hard to hear: No premade pie will ever taste as good as a homemade one.

It primarily comes down to the crust. Frozen and pre-baked pies typically rely on vegetable-based fat instead of butter because they’re more affordable, reliable, and shelf-stable—but that comes at a cost. You not only miss out on the decadent, buttery taste, but the crusts can also leave an unpleasant film on your tongue.

That stated, when you need to outsource to the grocery store, we found two options that will work in a pinch.

The pie that we’d feel most confident bringing to Thanksgiving dinner comes straight from the Whole Foods bakery department. That’s not to say it’s perfect, though. The crust is almost upsettingly pale, but it’s made with real butter and only a little bit of palm oil. And since it doesn’t leave a noticeable film and still lets the butter flavor shine, we’ll let this one slide.

Once you look past the crust’s color, this pie is solid overall. The filling is decadent, not too sweet, and creamy without being mushy. Whole Foods doesn’t shy away from the spices, either.

Senior Editor Samantha MacAvoy noted that the warming spices are nicely balanced, while Designer Alison Dominguez mentioned, “The flavor was exactly how a pumpkin pie should taste.”.

It has been revealed that costco’s pumpkin pie isn’t perfect: The crust uses palm oil-based shortening rather than butter and can develop a soggy bottom if you buy it too far in advance. (And it doesn’t hold a candle to the warehouse’s holy grail pumpkin cheesecake.) But it has a cult following for a reason, and not just because of its $5.99 price tag.

Even with its faults, the crust has great flavor and enough salt to create a balanced bite. Dominguez appreciated how it was “flaky and not too thick, and most importantly, it let the pie filling itself shine.” News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas chose Costco’s pie as her number one pick. “It all seemed to melt together in one creamy bite,” she said.

And at over three pounds, this dessert is the indisputable champion if you want to feed a crowd for less.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every cuisine has a sauce that’s an absolute essential—a ride or die, if you will. For South Asian food, this is a cilantro mint green chutney. It brings a punchy, herb-packed burst of flavor that goes with pretty much everything. This recipe combines cilantro, mint, and just the right amount of heat from green chiles, creating a balance of spice and freshness. Lime juice adds brightness, while cumin, sugar, and chaat masala add complexity. Use this as a zesty topping for your favorite dish or as a base for pani puri water (just add 1½ cups [360 ml] of water and strain), or make it creamy with yogurt or sour cream to use for spreading and dipping.

Slow-roasting Japanese sweet potatoes flesh-side down releases their natural sugars, caramelizing and deepening their sweetness. The flesh becomes incredibly tender, almost custard-like in texture, while the skin turns a rich golden brown and becomes slightly crispy. So don’t bother peeling them! Top them with tamarind concentrate (I like Tamicon, Cock Brand, Pure Indian Foods, or Dragonfly—anything without citric acid), green chutney, fresh onions, tomatoes, and cilantro for a chaat-inspired appetizer.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

According to recent reports, to a blender or food processor, add 2 bunches cilantro (about 6 oz. [170 g]), leaves and stems, 1 bunch mint (about 2 oz. [55 g]), leaves and tender stems, 6 green Thai chiles or 2 serranos, stemmed (more if you want it spicier), ½ cup (120 ml) lime juice (from about 5 limes), 2 tsp. cumin seeds, 1½ tsp. fine sea salt, 1 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. chaat masala. Pulse for a few seconds in intervals until the ingredients are pulverized into a smooth paste. Transfer to an airtight container and store until ready to use, up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Drizzle the sheet with extra-virgin olive oil and place 1½ lb. (680 g) Japanese or Korean sweet potatoes, ends trimmed, halved lengthwise, cut-side down. Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until golden and caramelized on the cut side and cooked through and tender; a knife inserted into the center of the potato should slide through easily. Let rest for 5 to 8 minutes. Once cool enough to handle, cut the sweet potatoes into 1" to 2" [2.5 to 5 cm] pieces.

To a small bowl, add ½ cup (120 g) plain whole-milk yogurt or sour cream and ½ tsp. fine sea salt and whisk to combine. If you’re using sour cream, thin it out with a little water.

Recent findings suggest that place the sweet potatoes on a serving platter and drizzle the yogurt, ½ cup Evergreen Chutney, 3 Tbsp. tamarind concentrate or paste, and 2 Tbsp. lime juice evenly all over. Sprinkle with 1 medium red tomato (5 oz. [140 g]), finely chopped, 1 small red onion (7 oz. [200 g]), finely chopped, 2 Tbsp. chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems, 1 tsp. chaat masala, 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, thinly sliced, and crispy sev and serve immediately.

Do Ahead: You can make the individual components a day ahead of time and store them in airtight containers in the refrigerator, then assemble to serve.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Introducing the Vogue Business People Moves Tracker, a running list highlighting the key executive appointments and exits across the fashion and beauty industries. From CEOs to creative directors to other key C-suite hires, we track the leadership shifts that are reshaping the industry.

Recent findings suggest that background: Therese Lundström has been appointed CMO of Isabel Marant. She previously served as chief marketing officer of Courrèges from 2023 to 2026. Her resume also includes Dries Van Noten and Givenchy.

Company comments: “Reporting directly to Catherine Jacquet, CEO of Isabel Marant, she will work closely with the teams to strengthen the brand’s global positioning, visibility and desirability,” according to a press release.

Sources indicate that background: Delphine Bellini has been appointed managing director of the upcoming Louis Vuitton landmark on the Champs-Élysées. In her new role, Bellini will oversee the creation and launch of the space. Bellini most recently served as CEO of Schiaparelli for the past 12 years.

Organization comments: “I am confident that Delphine’s vision and passion will bring our house’s highest ambitions to life in the heart of Paris,” Louis Vuitton chief commercial officer Hugues Bonnet-Masimbert mentioned in a statement.

“We are delighted to welcome Delphine. With her exceptional experience and the unwavering support of the entire EMEA team, we are confident that together we will make the 103 an extraordinary and iconic destination for the house,” EMEA zone president Francesco Viana added.

In a recent development, background: Alessandro Pungetti has been appointed head designer and creative director of Japanese brand White Mountaineering, starting with the FW27 season. Pungetti previously held roles as knitwear designer at Stone Island before joining CP Manufacturer as head designer across all collections. In 2009, he founded Ten C with Paul Harvey, who he previously collaborated with at Stone Island.

Company comments: “While inheriting the core values ​​of White Mountaineering, [Alessandro] will also pioneer new possibilities, leading to the brand’s further development,” the press release remarked.

Recent findings suggest that background: Justin Boxford has been appointed CEO of Capri Holdings, following John D Idol’s announcement that he will retire as chairman and CEO after two decades of leadership. Boxford joins from The Estée Lauder Companies, where he most recently served as global president, luxury beauty brands. He previously served as global brand president of Estée Lauder. To support the transition, Idol will serve as a senior advisor to Capri Holdings through March 31.

Sources indicate that tech giant comments: “We are confident that Justin is the right leader to guide Capri in its next chapter of growth,” said Robin Freestone, incoming independent chairman of the board. “He brings an exceptional track record of revitalizing and growing global luxury and beauty brands, deep international experience and a people-centered leadership approach.”.

According to recent reports, “It has been an extraordinary privilege to lead Capri for the past 23 years,” said Idol. “I am immensely proud of what we have accomplished together. I have had the opportunity to work with Justin in the past while he helped build the Michael Kors fragrance business at The Estée Lauder Companies and have watched his successes over the years. I am confident he is the ideal person to lead Capri into the future.”.

It has been revealed that background: Jonatan Janmark has stepped down as CEO of Circulose (formerly Renewcell), with CFO Amanda Geijer appointed to lead the business in the interim. In 2024, textile-to-textile recycler Renewcell filed for bankruptcy, having struggled to get the brand buy-in needed to keep its commercial-scale production facility in Sweden afloat. Former McKinsey partner Janmark was appointed CEO the same year, after renaming the tech giant to Circulose under the ownership of private equity firm Altor. Now, Janmark has stepped down, having completed his mandate of securing enough brand partnerships to restart the production plant. Geijer will take over with the support of executive chair Helena Helmersson.

Industry observers note that company comments: “When Jonatan joined, Circulose had just been given a second chance. Since then, he has made Circulose a leading player in textile-to-textile recycling again. That has taken a lot of energy, creativity and teamwork. I have learnt a lot from working with Jonatan, and I want to thank him for everything he has built,” Helmersson stated in a statement. “For the upcoming phase, I am very pleased that Amanda, who knows the company and our intends well, has agreed to lead Circulose as interim CEO until a permanent CEO is in place.”.

Background: Caroline Deroche Pasquier joins Dior in a newly created role as director of press, VIP and cultural relations. She began her career at Saint Laurent before joining LVMH, where she worked at Louis Vuitton and Givenchy. During the last six years, Pasquier has led global communications for Bottega Veneta and then Versace. At Dior, she will work closely with the house’s creative director Jonathan Anderson, reporting to Olivier Bialobos, deputy managing director in charge of global communication and image.

Company comments: “[Deroche Pasquier’s] career spans communication, creative collaboration, international markets and cultural relationships, giving her a broad perspective on the development and expression of luxury brands,” the company stated in a statement.

Background: Oliver Timm has voluntarily stepped down from Hugo Boss, where he’s been both chief sales officer and deputy CEO since 2024, as well as the organization board. In the meantime, CEO Daniel Grieder, alongside CFO and COO Ivica Maric, will split Timm’s previous duties. Timm was initially appointed as chief sales officer in 2021, to oversee Hugo Boss’s two brands (Boss and Hugo), including wholesale, e-commerce, visual merchandizing, retail operations, and customer relations.

The announcement follows Hugo Boss’s 5% sales drop in Q3 — attributed to an ongoing turnaround at the company — and Frasers Group’s de-facto takeover of the company on October 23.

Company comments: “Oliver Timm and I have been working side by side throughout our careers for almost 30 years, and it is a great honor for me to look back on this time and the many moments we have shared. I will miss working alongside him,” said Grieder in a statement. “During his time at Hugo Boss, he has repositioned sales with a future-oriented omnichannel approach and a strong customer-centric mindset, making a significant contribution to our growth and digitalization. As I look back at these achievements, I wish him, also on behalf of the entire managing board, the very best for the future.”.

Michael Murray, Hugo Boss chair and Frasers Group CEO, also shared his appreciation: “On behalf of the supervisory board, I would like to thank Oliver Timm for his contribution to Hugo Boss over the past years. We appreciate his commitment and wish him all the best for his professional and personal future.”.

Background: Ben Hallam, most recently SVP of marketing at Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts, has been appointed as Lululemon’s chief brand officer. At the sportswear brand, Hallam will lead global brand marketing, brand creative, store experience, and community. He will join the tech giant’s senior leadership team and report to CEO Heidi O’Neill who joined in April 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the announcement comes after the appointments of Maggie Gauger as president and chief product officer and Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer. On Friday, the company also announced the appointment of Emily Sunderland as chief strategy officer, effective November 23. Sunderland joins from Boston Consulting Group and will report to chief financial officer Meghan Frank. Searches remain underway for a chief technology officer and a chief communications officer.

In a recent development, company comments: “Ben brings an exceptional combination of creative vision, commercial discipline, and experience transforming iconic, premium brands at scale,” O’Neill said in a statement. “His proven ability to translate brand strategy into distinctive and compelling guest experiences will be critical as we strengthen how our brand comes to life across every touchpoint. Ben will play a central role in building a stronger and more competitive Lululemon.”.

Background: Daisy Shaw-Ellis has been appointed CMO of Malone Souliers, where she will oversee the brand’s global marketing and communications, with an emphasis on expansion in North America. Shaw-Ellis joins from Condé Nast, where she was most recently accessories and jewelry director for Vogue and Vanity Fair.

Organization comments: “We are delighted to welcome Daisy to Malone Souliers as global chief marketing officer,” CEO Andrew Wright said in a statement. “Her experience in executive positions at some of the industry’s most established and influential titles, alongside her exceptional eye and proven track record in luxury brand-building, will both enhance and amplify our voice globally. This is a pivotal moment for Malone Souliers as we embark on a upcoming and exciting trajectory, and we look forward to presenting the brand in new and exciting ways in the coming seasons.”.

Sources indicate that background: Clarisse Godbillon, who was CFO and COO of Lemaire from 2020 to 2025, is returning to the brand as managing director. She left Lemaire in 2025 to become COO of Jacquemus, and made the move back to the French label after Laetitia Mergui stepped down from the head job earlier this year.

Sources indicate that company comments: “Clarisse possesses an in-depth understanding of the company’s various activities and a profound knowledge of its identity,” the house said in a statement. “As managing director, she will oversee the development of the brand and lead its strategic and operational direction, working closely with [the house’s artistic directors and majority shareholders] Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-linh Tran.”.

Background: Lady Gaga has moved into the CEO role at Haus Labs, the clean beauty tech giant she founded in 2019. This comes after co-founder and former CEO Ben Jones exited the brand in early October. Gaga will now lead all commercial aspects of Haus Labs, alongside her prior responsibilities of creative direction and product development.

Sources indicate that background: Ryan Lally has been promoted to chief brand communications officer at Ralph Lauren Corp. Formerly SVP of global public relations and brand communications, Lally will continue to build on the organization’s global comms strategy in this newly created role, while overseeing talent partnerships, events and more. Lally has been with the company for more than two decades, and will continue to report to David Lauren, chief branding and innovation officer.

Sources indicate that background: Alexis Hoopes, formerly global fashion VP at Ebay, has joined The RealReal as chief merchandising officer. At Ebay, she led the tech giant’s $10 billion global fashion business for two-plus years, including the expansion of its Authenticity Guarantee program to new categories, price points and markets, strengthening trust among buyers and sellers. Hoopes will now lead The RealReal’s merchandising strategy, focusing on its luxury assortment and personalized product discovery — as the platform further advances its AI capabilities and unlocks growth opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that firm comments: “Alexis is a proven leader who brings a rare combination of luxury merchandising expertise, global marketplace experience and operational discipline,” Rati Sahi Levesque, president and CEO of The RealReal, noted in a statement. “As we build on our leadership in luxury resale, her ability to connect exceptional merchandise with evolving consumer demand will be instrumental in accelerating growth.”.

Industry observers note that background: Hector Muelas joined LVMH in 2015 as global VP of content and creative, after working for Apple. Between 2017 and 2019, he was chief brand officer of LVMH-owned luggage brand Rimowa under chief executive Alexandre Arnault. Muelas then returned to Apple as global group creative director in 2019, a role he held until 2021. He returned to LVMH in 2023 as Tiffany & Co.’s global chief brand and creative officer, reuniting with Alexandre Arnault.

He has now been named Louis Vuitton chief brand creative officer, a newly created position reporting to Louis Vuitton deputy CEO Damien Bertrand.

Industry observers note that organization comments: “Hector will define and steer our creative storytelling across all touchpoints, thereby ensuring strong overall image consistency. Leading creative and content execution, he will oversee all brand campaigns, with the art buying team led by Magena Chansarel and the content factory team led by Carole Fuchs joining his organization. In close collaboration with our business units, regions, and creative talents, Hector will further elevate our brand desirability, ensuring the house continues to set the benchmark in cultural resonance, creative boldness, and emotional connection with our clients worldwide,” Bertrand noted in an internal announcement.

Background: Bruno Pavlovsky, who most recently exited the board at Chanel, but remains president of Chanel SAS and fashion, is now co-chair of The Fashion Pact. A non-profit organization, The Fashion Pact is a coalition of CEOs from more than 150 companies representing a third of the global fashion industry by volume. Pavlovsky will work alongside Inditex CEO Óscar García Maceiras and climate campaigner Paul Polman to build on the work of the pact in creating a net-zero fashion industry. (Chanel is among the coalition’s founding signatories back in 2019.).

Manufacturer comments: “As we look ahead to 2027, our focus is increasingly on translating collective ambition into implementation, and scaling solutions across the industry. Bruno’s appointment marks an notable step in this journey, bringing valuable leadership and perspective as we work to strengthen collaboration across regions, business models and supply chains,” The Fashion Pact wrote on LinkedIn.

It has been revealed that background: Bruno Pavlovsky joined Chanel in 1990 and became a board member in 2018, a duty he will now step down from. Since 2022, he has also been president of the Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode. Pavlovsky remains president of Chanel SAS and of the house’s fashion activities.

Sources indicate that company comments: “This latest move marks the completion of the board’s evolution toward a composition of independent directors, bringing diverse external expertise and perspectives, while retaining executive representation through the global executive chair and global CEO. Bruno Pavlovsky remains fully committed to his role as president of Chanel’s fashion activities and president of Chanel SAS,” Chanel remarked in a statement.

Background: Zankov has appointed Jack Tobin, founder of luxury brand development consultancy Jack Tobin Agency, as CEO and business partner of Zankov, formalizing a partnership that has developed since Tobin began consulting for the brand two years ago. Since beginning its partnership with Jack Tobin Agency, Zankov has increased its international business more than tenfold and doubled its global stockist network.

According to recent reports, tech giant comments: “Zankov is at an incredibly exciting stage in its growth. I have always envisioned having a partner who could join me in shaping the next chapter of the brand — someone who shares my ambition to build an enduring business while staying true to the creative vision that has always defined Zankov. Jack is the ideal partner to take this next step with, and I’m excited about what we can build together,” states Henry Zankov, founder and creative director.

Background: Net-a-Porter (NAP) has appointed Devina Foley as Americas president to oversee the retailer’s US and Canada strategy. With more than 20 years of experience across retail, merchandising and e-commerce, Foley will help strengthen NAP’s market positioning as it settles into a new era under LuxExperience Group. She has held senior leadership roles at Bandier, Rockets of Awesome and Gilt, following earlier positions at Loft and Gap Inc. Based in New York, Foley will report to NAP CEO Heather Kaminetsky.

Sources indicate that company comments: “Devina brings an impressive breadth of experience and a proven track record of driving growth and leading businesses through transformation,” Kaminetsky said in a statement. “Her leadership and expertise will be invaluable as we continue to grow Net-a-Porter’s US business.”.

Background: LVMH has promoted Clara Boissonnas, formerly women’s leather goods product director at Louis Vuitton, to CEO of Pucci. Boissonnas joined Louis Vuitton in 2002 as a product manager, before exiting four years later. After a decade working across Lanvin and Byredo, she returned to LV where she helped shape the maison’s coveted leather goods business. At Pucci, Boissonnas will strengthen the brand’s distinctive creative identity, desirability, and international reach, while reporting to Pietro Beccari, chair and CEO of the LVMH Fashion Group. As for Saar Debrouwere, who has led Pucci since 2022, her future role will be declared in due course, according to the group.

Recent findings suggest that tech giant comments: “Clara has made a significant contribution to Louis Vuitton through her deep product expertise, strong creative sensibility, and unwavering commitment to excellence. Her ability to combine creative ambition with a clear understanding of the business makes her ideally suited to lead Pucci into its next chapter,” Beccari stated in a statement.

Background: Yanina Novitskaya, who has spent the last 19 years at Cartier, most recently as CEO of South East Asia and Oceania, is the next chief executive of Richemont-owned Delvaux. Delvaux, the world’s oldest fine leather goods house, was founded in Brussels in 1829. In its next chapter, Novitskaya succeeds Jean-Marc Loubier, who returned to lead the brand after its acquisition in 2021, and will report to Richemont fashion and accessories CEO Philippe Fortunado.

Company comments: “Yanina’s strong knowledge of the luxury industry will be instrumental in leading Delvaux into its next chapter, strengthening its distinctive positioning and continuing to drive product desirability and international growth,” Fortunato noted in a statement.

It has been revealed that background: Marc Jacobs has appointed John Wattiker as CMO to lead the brand’s global marketing strategy. Wattiker joins the brand after almost 15 years at Hearst Magazines working in the company’s advertising business, where he most recently held the role of VP of fashion and luxury.
